title: Chapter XXXII
summary: Jane's school flourishes as she learns the individual capacities of her pupils and earns the neighborhood's affection, though dreams still return her to Rochester. Through Rosamond's visits and portrait, Jane makes St. John confess that he loves Rosamond intensely but considers her unfit for missionary life and predicts regret after a year of marriage. He chooses his grand design over available domestic happiness. While examining the portrait, St. John secretly tears away a scrap on which Jane has written her real surname.
events: Jane's pupils progress, and useful work brings her social regard and daily peace.
Rosamond's visits expose St. John's continuing passion despite his control.
Jane urges St. John to marry Rosamond, but he judges her incompatible with his missionary ambition.
St. John notices Jane's true name on a scrap associated with Rosamond's portrait and carries it away.

characters.name: Jane Eyre
characters.development: Turns principled duty into reciprocal affection and meaningful achievement while remaining emotionally alive to Rochester.

characters.name: St. John Rivers
characters.development: Consciously sacrifices the woman he loves because neither love nor domestic good can satisfy his heroic religious ambition.

characters.name: Rosamond Oliver
characters.development: Her affection is genuine and socially possible, but her temperament is unsuited to the role St. John has made absolute.

threads.text: Jane succeeds in the independent vocation St. John found for her.
St. John rejects Rosamond and preserves his missionary course.
The Jane Elliott alias is compromised when St. John finds the name Jane Eyre.
